sources.title: The inner sense of time: how the brain creates a representation of duration
The time-emotion paradox
sources.publisher: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences, 364(1525), 1943-1953

concepts.definition: A duration estimate made while one knows that time will be judged.
A duration estimate made afterwards from memory.

questions.q: Why does a novel holiday seem long in memory?
questions.a: It creates many distinct memories, and the number of memories shapes remembered duration.

questions.q: What does arousing emotion do to felt duration?
questions.a: It tends to lengthen it, as if the internal pace is faster.
